title: Coalesce Missing Department Name
description:
Join employees to their department. If an employee has no department, display `'Unassigned'` instead of NULL.

**Table: employees**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| department_id | INT |

**Table: departments**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |

Output columns: `employee_name`, `department_name`. Order by `employee_name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE departments (id INT, name VARCHAR); INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1, 'Engineering'), (2, 'Sales'); CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, department_id INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1, 'Alice', 1), (2, 'Bob', 2), (3, 'Carol', NULL), (4, 'Dan', NULL), (5, 'Eve', 1);
solution_sql: SELECT e.name AS employee_name, COALESCE(d.name, 'Unassigned') AS department_name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id ORDER BY employee_name

test_cases.description: Carol and Dan show Unassigned; others show their department

hints: LEFT JOIN returns all employees, even those without a department (d.name will be NULL).
COALESCE(value, fallback) returns value if it is not NULL, otherwise returns fallback.
explanation: After the LEFT JOIN, employees without a department have `d.name = NULL`. `COALESCE(d.name, 'Unassigned')` replaces that NULL with the string `'Unassigned'`.
